name: Creality Falcon T1 20W Diode
tagline: 2026 modular galvo workstation: swap diode, fiber, MOPA, or UV heads
tldr: Creality's Falcon T1 (global launch May 2026) is a Class 1 enclosed galvo platform with swappable WaveSync modules: 20W/40W diode, 20W fiber, 60W MOPA, and 5W UV. Buy the base once, add laser types as your shop grows: competes with xTool F1/F2 Ultra on flexibility rather than fixed dual-laser boxes.
mainObjective: Modular enclosed galvo for makers who want one chassis and multiple laser types

priceRange.note: Official Creality store, Oct 2026: $2,499, complete machine

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: All modules at once: one head installed

pros: Cheapest way into the T1 platform: $2,499 on Creality's store (October 2026)
Galvo engraving: much faster fills than a gantry diode of similar power
Tool-free module swap in about 15 seconds when you add other laser types
cons: Cutting depth limited to about 8 mm basswood (Creality rating)
Galvo field of about 220 × 220 mm: smaller than gantry machines at this price
Modules bought later need calibration before first use
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Creality Falcon T1 Diode. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Price the full module roadmap before buying: T1 plus fiber and MOPA can exceed a single F2 Ultra bundle.
primaryUse: 2026 modular galvo production platform for shops that want to expand laser types without replacing the entire machine.

moduleSystem.headline: WaveSync swappable galvo modules
moduleSystem.description: One enclosed T1 chassis accepts Creality diode (20W/40W), fiber (20W), MOPA (60W), and UV (5W) modules: install one head at a time.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 20W diode module is the sensible entry to Creality's WaveSync platform: Class 1 galvo enclosure, wood and leather revenue, and a chassis that later accepts fiber, MOPA, or UV heads without replacing the whole machine.
editorialDepth.limitations: Galvo field is smaller than open-frame diode beds. Module swaps mean downtime between material types. Price the full module roadmap before buying: fiber and MOPA add up quickly.

faq.question: What can the Falcon T1 20W diode cut?
faq.answer: Creality lists up to 8 mm basswood and 6 mm opaque acrylic for the 20W diode module (figures reported by Igor's Lab from Creality). As a galvo, it is quicker at engraving than at cutting: our benchmark put a 10 × 10 cm cut-out in 3 mm basswood at about 6–10 min.

faq.question: How much do the Falcon T1 and its extra modules cost?
faq.answer: On Creality's US store in October 2026 the T1 with the 20W diode was $2,499 (it launched at $2,249). Modules sold alone: 40W diode $1,399, 20W fiber $1,099, 5W UV $2,599, 60W MOPA $2,699. Modules bought separately must be calibrated before first use.

faq.question: Should I start the T1 with the 20W diode or the 40W?
faq.answer: Start with the 20W if the T1 is mainly for engraving wood, leather and coated items and you plan to add a fiber or UV module next. Start with the 40W bundle ($2,999, $500 more) if cutting wood is the main job: Creality rates it 12 mm basswood and 10 mm opaque acrylic.

standoutFeatures.title: One enclosure, five laser types
standoutFeatures.body: The T1 takes diode, fiber, MOPA and UV WaveSync modules, swapped without tools in about 15 seconds according to Creality.

standoutFeatures.title: Entry ticket to the platform
standoutFeatures.body: The 20W diode bundle is the lowest-priced T1 and leaves room in the budget for a metal or UV module later.
